key_insight: The paper focuses on making EEG-based ADHD feature comparisons more consistent through standardized data preparation. Its curated collection includes 669 existing BALLADEER recordings from 156 participants across five task conditions.
problem_solved: Differences in EEG preparation, analysis windows and recording-quality decisions can undermine fair comparisons of features used to classify ADHD in children and adolescents.
method: Curate existing BALLADEER EEG recordings spanning five task conditions.
Use consistent signal preparation and shared analysis windows to support comparable feature analysis.
Document recording-quality decisions to make the evaluation process more transparent.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, consistent preprocessing can support more reproducible feature evaluation for EEG-based ADHD classification. The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific feature findings and classification performance cannot be confirmed.
visual_elements: Dataset overview: 669 recordings → 156 participants → 5 task conditions.
Pipeline diagram: EEG recordings → consistent preparation → shared windows → feature comparison.
Aligned EEG traces illustrating a common analysis window.
Quality-control checklist highlighting documented recording decisions.
paper_title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
paper_authors: Javier Sanchis, Álvaro Navarro, Jorge García-Carrasco, Tahar Kechadi, Juan Trujillo
